Test what you can remember before looking at your notes.

1. Read a short section and close your notes.

2. Write three questions and answer them from memory.

3. Check the answers and correct gaps. Try those questions again in a later session.
Return to material across several study sessions.

1. Split a topic into small sections.

2. Plan reviews on different days, for example tomorrow, in three days and next week.

3. Start each review with a short self-test. Adjust the gaps to your deadline.
Mix related problem types after learning the basic methods.

1. Work through an example of each method first.

2. Mix a few older problem types into your practice.

3. Before solving each problem, explain which method fits and why.
Explain why a worked example uses each step.

1. Choose a worked example from your course.

2. Describe each step in your own words and connect it to a rule or principle.

3. Solve a similar problem without copying the example, then check your reasoning.
